'''Ivan McFarlin''' (born April 26, 1982) is an American  former professional [[basketball]] player.

==Basketball career==
McFarlin attended [[Willowridge High School (Houston)|Willowridge High School]] in [[Houston]], Texas, where he led his team to win the state championship in his senior year, as he averaged 15.9 points, 14.9 rebounds, 3.5 blocks and 3.2 steals. McFarlin played [[college basketball]] at [[Oklahoma State University]], and helped the Cowboys to a Final Four appearance in 2004, where the team lost to [[Georgia Tech]] on a late-game basket. He is one of four Oklahoma State players to have over 1,000 points, 700 rebounds, and 100 blocks,<ref name=bendigoadvertiser/> the other three being [[Byron Houston]], [[Leroy Combs]] and [[Bryant Reeves]].

In the [[2006-07 NBA season]], McFarlin was a member of the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], but was traded on December 19, 2006, along with NBA superstar [[Allen Iverson]] for two [[NBA draft|draft]] picks, [[Andre Miller]] and [[Joe Smith (basketball)|Joe Smith]]. He was immediately waived.<ref>[https://www.denverpost.com/sports/ci_4890334 The Denver Post - Injury bug hits team once again<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

McFarlin later played in Poland with SKK Kotwica [[Kołobrzeg|Kolobrzeg]].<ref name=eurobasket>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=SUI&PlayerID=45667&AmNotSure=1|title = Ivan McFarlin Player Profile, Bendigo Braves, News, Stats - australiabasket}}</ref> In 2010, he played for the [[Bendigo Braves]] of the [[South East Australian Basketball League]].<ref name=bendigoadvertiser>[https://www.bendigoadvertiser.com.au/news/local/sport/football-australian-rules/mcfarlin-fits-the-braves-bill/1742955.aspx McFarlin fits the Braves' bill - Local News - Sport - Football - Australian Rules - The Advertiser]</ref> He made the league's all star team and led the league in rebounds and rebounds per game.

Prior to the 2010/2011 season, he signed with [[Hapoel Lev HaSharon]] of the  [[Israel]]i [[Liga Leumit (basketball)|Liga Leumit]].<ref>[http://safsal.co.il/hplayer.aspx?id=32606 Player profile @ Safsal.co.il] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721140817/http://safsal.co.il/hplayer.aspx?id=32606 |date=July 21, 2011 }} (in [[Hebrew]])</ref>

In 2011 Ivan returned to the Bendigo Braves.

After spending 2012 playing in China, the [[Bendigo Braves]] announced that Ivan would be returning to play a third season with the Braves in 2013.

==Personal life==
McFarlin is the son of Delphine and Tyrone Powell McFarlin, of Missouri City, Texas.<ref name=eurobasket/>
He currently lives in Stillwater, Oklahoma, the town of his college alma mater, Oklahoma State University, and assists the Oklahoma State basketball program. McFarlin also works part-time elsewhere. On May 22, 2019, McFarlin was named the head coach of the Ponca City Boys High School basketball team in Oklahoma. In 2023 McFarlin was named the head coach of the Agra High school and Middle School basketball team.
